ALBERT S. GARCIA Governor Bataan Dear Governor Garcia: This has reference to your letter dated IO March 2016 requesting for an advice on whether the sanggunians of the different levels of local government units (LGUs) may pass ordinances for the selection of sectoral representatives whose salary and emoluments shall be included in their own appropriation? If not, you also asked on how the provisions of the Local Government Code on sectoral representations to the sanggunian be given life in the light of these circumstances? Per your letter, you already posed the same query before DILG-Region III where Director Florida Dijan in a letter dated 03 February 2016 made a prompt reply, thus: "xxx we regret to inform you that as of date, there still is no law providing for the manner of electing the sectoral representatives in all the local sanggunias as provided under the Local Government Code of 1991 save for the indigenous cultural minorities. Among the different sectors mentioned in the Local Government Code, only the sector of' indigenous cultural minorities has an enabling law to install them in the different sanggunians. Similarly, there is yet no implementing rules or guidelines pertaining to the organization of the women, agricultural and industrial workers, and urban poor and disabled persons from which their representatives may be selected and/or nominated. " Hence, your subject letter-appeal to the Central Office. We maintain the position of RD Dijan on the matter as embodied in her letter dated 03 February 2016 to Mr. Aurelio C. Angeles, Jr., Provincial Legal Officer, Province of Bataan. In order to elucidate our position on the matter, may we invite your attention to the following provisions of Republic Act No. 7160 or the Local Government Code of 1991 , to wit:

Section 41 (b) and (c) of the local Government Code of 1991 "SECTION 41. The presidents of the leagues of sanggunian members of component cities and municipalities shall serve as ex-officio members of the sangguniang panla/a wigan concerned. The presidents of the liga ng mga barangay and the pederasyon ng Inga sangguniang kabataan elected by their respective chapters, as provided in this Code, shall serve as ex-officio members of the sangguniang panlalawigan, sangguniang panlungsod, and sangguniang bayan. The COMELEC shall romul ate the rules andre ulationstoeffective/ rovidefortheelection of such sectoral representatives. " (Emphasis Supplied) Section 446 of the Local Government Code of 1991 SEC. 446. Composition.—(a) The sangguniang bayan, the legislative body of the municipality, shall be composed of the m unicipal vice-mayor as the presiding officer, the regular sanggunian members, the president of the municipal chapter of the liga ng Inga barangay, the president of the of the municipal chapter of the liga ng mga barangay, the president of the pambayang pederasyon ng mga sanggunang kabataan, and the sectoral representtaives, as members. In addition thereto, there shall be three (3) sectoral (b) representatives: one (I) from the women; and, as shall be determined by the sanggunian concerned within ninety (90) days prior to the holding of the local elections, one (l) from the agricultural or industrial workers; and one (1) from the other sectors, including the urban poor, indigenous cultural minorities, or disabled persons. (c) The reg ular mem bers of th e sanggun iang bayan an d sectoral representatives shall be elected in the manner as may be provided for b v law. " (Emphasis Supplied)

Section 457 of the Local Government Code of 1991 "SEC. 457. Composition.- (a) The sangguniang panlungsod, the legislative body OT the city, shall be composed OT the city vice-mayor as presiding officer, the regular sanggunian members, the president of the city chapter of the liga ng mga barangay, the president of the panlungsod na pederasyon ng mga sangguniang kabataan, and the sectoral representatives, as members. In addition thereto, there shall be three (3) sectoral (b) representatives: one (1) from the women; and, as shall be determined by the sanggunian concerned within ninety (90) days prior to the holding of the local elections, one (l) from the agricultural or industrial workers; and one (I) from the other sectors, including the urban poor, indigenous cultural minorities, or disa bled persons. (c) The regular members of the sangguniang panlungsod and sectoral representatives shall be elected in the manner as may be provided for by " (Emphasis Supplied) Section 467 of the Local Government Code of 1991 'SEC. 467. Composition.- (a) The sangguniang panlalavvigan, the legislative body of the province, shall be composed of' the provincial vice governor as presiding officer, the regular sanggunian members, the president of the provincial chapter of the liga ng mga barangay, the president of the panlalawigang pederasyon ng mga sangguniang kabataan, the president of the provincial federation of' the sanggunian members of municipalities and component cities, and the sectoral representatives, as members. In addition thereto, there shall be three (3) sectoral (b) representatives: one (l) from the women; and, as shall be determined by the sanggunian concerned within ninety (90) days prior to the holding of the local elections, one (l) from the agricultural or industrial workers; and one (I) from the other sectors, including the urban poor, indigenous cultural minorities, or disabled persons. (c) The regular members of the sangg uniang panlala wigan an d the sectoral representatives shall be elected in the manner at; mav be provided Tor bv la w. " (Emphasis Supplied)

Based on Section 41 (C) of the Local Government Code of 1991, the sangguniang bayan, sangguniang panlungsod and sangguniang panlalawigan, in addition to the regular and ex-officio members, shall be further composed of three (3) sectoral representatives. It is noted that in the aforesaid Section 41 (b), the sectors for women and workers are already assured of one seat each. With respect to the other sectors, such as the urban poor, indigenous cultural communities, disabled persons or any other sector, the sanggunian shall determine within ninety (90) days prior to the holding of the next local elections which sector from among the other sectors shall be represented in their respective sanggunians. However, Section 41 (C) of the Local Government Code of 1991 has to be reconciled with Sections 446 (c), 457 (c) and 467 (c) of the same Code with respect to the composition of the sangguniang bayan, sangguniang panlungsod and sangguniang panlalawigan, respectively. Sections 446 (c), 457 (c) and 467 (c) of the Code provides that the sectoral representatives of the sangguniang panlalawigan, sangguniang panlungsod and sangguniang bayan, respectively, shall be elected in the manner as may be provided for by law. The phrase "as may be provided for by law "entails that Congress should pass another law that will provide the other details regarding the election of local sectoral representatives. Such requirement of an enabling law was reiterated by Congress when it enacted in 1995 Republic Act No. 78871 which, in part, states that: "The Commission shall promulgate rules and regulations to effectively implement the provisions of law which ma v hereafter be enacted providing for the election ofsectoral representatives. "(Emphasis Supplied) While there are already pending bills in Congress, as of this date, it has not yet passed a law providing for the manner of electing the sectoral representatives in the sanggunians as mandated under the Local Government Code of 1991. This would answer why there are still no sectoral representatives in all the Sanggunians, for that matter, as provided for by the Local Government Code of 1991. Meantime, on 29 October 1997, Republic Act No. 8371, otherwise known as the Indigenous Peoples Rights Act of 1997 (hereinafter "RA 8371") was approved and signed into law. Said law recognizes the policy of the State in affording the indigenous people communities adequate representations in the local government sanggunians at all levels. Precisely, pursuant to Section 6, Rule IV of the Implementing Rules and Regulations of RA 8371, it is mandated that indigenous peoples shall be represented in all sanggunians at all levels whose representatives shall be selected in accordance with the customs and traditions of the indigenous people concerned. Along this line, it is noted that it was the Entitled "AN Acr INSrrrtJ1'1NG ELECTORAL REFORMS FOR THE PURPOSE OF AMENDING SECTION 3, PARAGRAPHS (C) AND (D) OF REPUBHC Acr NO. 7166".

NCIP, which was mandated by law to come up with the Implementing Rules and Regulations. The Department has consistently opined that RA 8371 and its Implementing Rules and Regulations issued by the NCIP are already sufficient as an enabling law to install the indigenous peoples representatives in the different sanggunians of LGUs. Hence, among the different sectors mentioned in Sections 41 (C) and, 446 (b), 457 (b) and 467 (b) of the Local Government Code of 1991, only the sector of indigenous cultural minorities has an enabling law to install them in the different sanggunians of LGUs. Finally, as to the question on how the provisions of the Local Government Code of 1991 on sectoral representations to the sanggunian be given life in the light of these circumstances, since what is missing is the enactment of a law that would clearly enable sectors mentioned in the Local Government Code of 1991 to be represented in the legislative bodies of local governments, then your are advised to further strengthen or reinforce manifestations and/or lobbying in Congress for a law that will finally put the Constitutional mandate into effect. Thank you. Very ly yours, AUSTERE A. PANADERO Undersecretary • OUSIG 2016 -22-01 Ls/17 Copy furnished: DIR. FLORIDA M. DIJAN Regional Director, DILG-Region Brgy.
